# Rime Lords · Book II, pp. 316–331
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	316
P	In the utmost north, the Rime Lords made their domain. They spread through the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480) and the tundra beyond, embracing the ice and the cold and the terrible howling emptiness.
P	The Rime Lords developed all manner of ascetic disciplines and esoteric arts. They inured their bodies to the cold.
P	They sent their minds wandering through spirit realms.
P	They shaped matter and energy with their will, imposed stillness on the world, froze pockets of reality in timeless stasis.
P	Disciples came from the farm-valleys and the mammoth herders, to study at the feet of these living gods. Their teachings were harsh, rigorous, and demanding. But for a time, monasteries dotted the north and the ways of the Rime Lords flourished.
P	But then the servants of the <b>Stone</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 382) rebelled and set loose the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).
P	Something cracked open at the very roof of the world, and the voice of Y'aaw'kara (the Howling Wind, the Flayer of Flesh) was unleashed.
P	Bloodthirst and madness spread.
PAGE	317
P	Some Rime Lords fell to the <b>Howling</b> <b>Curse</b> (page 492). Others were brought low by mortal mobs run rampant. The thirteen survivors agreed that something must be done. They each retreated to a place of power, sent forth their minds, and together sealed the rift beneath a glacier of <b>dark ice</b> (page 322), quieting Y'aaw'kara's voice.
P	The Howling Curse dulled to a constant whisper. But the last thirteen Rime Lords had sacrificed themselves. Their bodies remain encased in ice, their minds working the magic intended to keep Y'aaw'kara's voice at bay for eternity.
H2	Names
HR
P	Sanskrit-inspired: Akativet, Artarapishi, Dahishika, Goranat, Kanishanu, Mamaranu, Marash, Nilani, Prayanavi, Ralananan, Ranaji, Shayand, Supnam, Vitatana
P	Often combined with a title of "Gar"
P	("teacher") or appellations of "Div" ("the holy") or Kav ("the wise"). For example "Gar Akativet," "Kanishanu Div," or "Ranaji Kav."

B	A new glacier starts to form in the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480), spreading into the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200) and upsetting the spirits there

H3	Thoughtform
P	Objects, sensations, or vignettes of manifest will, formed of base matter or energy, like how a spirit manifests a body. Not real, but real enough.
B	A grand tree, growing in a lightless cave. Its bark and wood are shaped of stone, but its petals/leaves/fruits crumble to dust and water when shed.
B	A bubble of stillness on a wind-swept summit, boasting an elaborately decorated altar. The altar is flimsy as frost, dissolving if touched.
B	A chant that fills a valley, echoing endlessly from the mountainsides.
B	A spring in a low valley, the water never freezing. Drinking vessels are found at the water's edge, impossibly beautiful, but melting into water if removed.

H2	Dark ice
HR
P	Purplish ice, which stays cold and frozen except in the hottest furnace. The Rime Lords could form and shape it at will.
P	Some of their disciples learned the trick, too, but the art has largely been lost.
P	Pick or roll for form and characteristic.
P	<b>1d12</b> form
HR
P	1-3 Fragment (chip/shard/chunk/etc.), from something larger
P	4-5 Enigmatic shape (cube/sphere/spiral/etc.), its purpose unclear
P	6-7 Mundane object (tool/utensil/ container/etc.), though perhaps not easily recognized as such
P	8-9 Art or decoration (jewel/statue/ tiles/torc/amulet/ring/etc.)
P	10-12 Construction (door/stairway/arch/ bricks/walls/etc.), likely <i>immobile</i> Consider rolling 1d6 to inform size/scale.
P	1d12 characteristic
HR
P	1 Breathtakingly beautiful
P	2 Dims light/color in its presence
P	3 Absorbs/baffles sound
P	4 Exceptionally hard, roll 1d6 for degree (otherwise, hard as mundane ice)
P	5 Presents a tangible barrier to spirits, even when unmanifest
P	6 Pieces persist when removed, instead of melting like normal ice
P	7-8 Roll 1d6 twice and combine
P	9-12 Just (just) a bit of never-melting ice Consider rolling 1d6 to inform how pristine the dark ice is.

H3	A column of ice
P	<i>magical</i>, <i>immobile</i>
P	Amidst a high, lonely meadow stands a pillar of dark purple ice, 12 feet tall and 2 feet thick. It rests on a circular slab of rune-etched stone, a dozen paces across, untouched by time or nature. There's a stillness to the place, a tension in the air.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> The runes appear to be some sort of spell, waiting to be triggered; it'd take days of study to puzzle out the command word (and you risk triggering it accidentally).
P	<b>Something useful:</b> You can determine the command word with a few hours of study (less if you're versed in Rime Lord script).
P	When you <b><i>speak the command word near</i></b> <b><i>the column</i></b>, the dark ice expands in a flash, encasing the stone slab and anything on it.
P	The ice traps even spirits (manifest or not).
P	Mortal prisoners soon perish, their souls ensnared. The dark ice never melts and resists all but the mightiest magic and blows.

H3	A dark ice knife
P	<i>hand</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>crude</i>
P	A hilt of bone, with a spike of dark ice tapering to a sharp point. The ice is hard as stone, and not especially sharp.
P	When you <b><i>stab an undead entity with the</i></b> <b><i>knife</i></b>, ask the GM whether it is driven by obsession, hunger, and/or vengeance. If the answer is "yes," then deal +1d4 damage (ignores armor), and leave the entity briefly disoriented. Should this reduce the entity to 0 HP, the dark ice knife melts away along with whatever bound the entity to this world.

H2	Tulpa
HR
P	A tulpa is a constructed <b>spirit</b> (page 356), created by the powerful will of another. The Rime Lords crafted many such entities, which linger on in their creators' wake.
P	A tulpa has the <i>spirit</i> and <i>construct</i> tags, with a move that reflects them manifesting or possessing a physical form. They are animated by more than biology (+4 HP) and usually lack vital organs (+3 HP, +1 Armor). Pick or roll a purpose, size, ability, tether, and disposition. Use these elements to inform how it manifests and behaves.

P	7-8 Curiosity/instruction/assistance/ practice
P	9-10 Something obscure, or very specific
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 twice, combine

P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs) or 4 vs.
P	stabbing (just bones)
P	<b>Damage</b> bony fingers d4 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to one specific bone <b>Instinct</b> to keep their master's house in order
P	• Animate its particular skeleton
P	• Grab on and pull them down with numbers
P	• Reassemble themselves (regaining 1d4 HP), unless their tether is shattered
P	Some of the simplest tulpas to create, each of these spirits is bound to a skeleton that's been stripped of flesh and intricately carved. The Rime Lords and their disciples used them as domestic servants, tending to material needs and serving as guardians when needed. Gingkara still attempt to preserve their master's homes, for what else should they do with their existence?

H3	Khyagseng
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>resolute</i>, <i>observant</i>, <i>fierce</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 13; <b>Armor</b> 2 (icy "skin," lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> icy jaws and paws d8+2 with advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to its pedestal; body made of dark ice; cold-proof
P	<b>Instinct</b> to repel intruders
P	• See through illusions and deceptions
P	• Offer a rumbling (though polite) warning
P	• Repair itself while on its pedestal
P	These tulpas inhabit dark-ice sculptures of three-eyed, stylized lions—muscular, proud, fierce—standing atop decorated pedestals. Always found in pairs, guarding doorways or thresholds. They dutifully challenge any who approach without an invitation from their master. Never mind that their masters are all long gone.
P	Some of the grander Rime Lord ruins boast large khyagseng made of dark ice that is strong as stone (+8 HP, +1 Armor, +1 damage). These greater guardians can also unleash a thunderous roar, deafening and terrifying, likely to trigger avalanches.

H3	Mkhalang
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>huge</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>devious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 27; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> trample d8+3 with disadvantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>) or ice-tusks d8+7 with disadvantage (<i>reach</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>, <i>crude</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to its dome but far-ranging; perfect memory; unable to lie <b>Instinct</b> to amuse itself at the expense of others
P	• Fly quickly across the skies
P	• Manifest a mammoth-like form of freezing mist and ice (harmed only by salt, fire, heat)
P	• Suck the strength and warmth from anyone they trample
P	• Reveal just enough to cause trouble
P	The Rime Lords created these mighty spirits to act as emissaries and spies. A few still remain, tethered to the meditation-halls in which they were made but roaming the Whitefangs in search of novelty and diversion. They have grown bored in their masters' absence, and from boredom has grown a subtle cruelty.
P	The people of the Whitefangs treat them with respect, for they are still the emissaries of the Rime Lords. But they also know better than to trust their counsel.

H3	Shaksa
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>hoarder</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> antler of jagged bone d10+2 (<i>close</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing) or stone hooves
P	d8 (<i>hand</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to its cemetery, can only leave to track looters/vandals <b>Instinct</b> to preserve the sanctity of the dead
P	• Fill an intruder with dread
P	• Manifest a form of bone and gravedirt (unharmed by stabbing; vulnerable to rain/running water)
P	• Track a looter or vandal, unerringly
P	The Rime Lords and their disciples created shaksa to guard over cemeteries and charnel grounds. They usually watch, unseen and unmanifest.
P	A shaksa manifests only within its cemetery, appearing as a powerful goat made of rock and soil, with a human (?) skull for a head, three eyes of floating light, and a single great antler of jagged bone. Once manifest, it can leave the cemetery in pursuit of looters or vandals. Should this form be destroyed, the spirit returns to the cemetery and cannot remanifest until the next sunset.

H3	Deadly cold
P	Rime Lord ruins sometimes include areas that are much, much colder than even the surrounding mountains. Dangerously, lethally cold.
P	• Show a warning: a subtle change in light/sound, breath or smoke condensing/freezing, hoarfrost
P	• Weigh them down with frost
P	• Have gear stick/freeze/break
P	• Inflict <b>hypothermia & frostbite</b> (page 489), quickly and with little warning

H3	Adept
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 2 (toughness, skill)
P	<b>Damage</b> freezing touch or aura d8 (<i>hand</i> or <i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> cold-proof; spirit sight; no longer ages; needs little food/drink/ sleep; powerful will
P	<b>Instinct</b> see below
P	• Send their mind forth into the spirit world, their bodies in stasis
P	• Reveal a teaching/technique of the
P	• 1-4 additional moves (next page)
P	The Rime Lords taught that the self could be perfected. That the needs and frailties of the body could be purged. That the mind could free itself of the flesh and know the unseen world of spirits and fundamental forces. That the will could conquer all. The goal was nothing short of immortality, the preservation of the perfect self.
P	For most of the Rime Lords' mortal disciples, these teachings did little more than strengthen the body and clear the mind. But for some—the adepts—these teachings unlocked a fragment of their masters' power.
P	Rivalries were fierce among the adepts even when the Rime Lords walked the land.
P	When the last Rime Lords disappeared, these rivalries flourished into schisms, sects, and violent purges. Some of the adepts fell.
P	Others went into hiding. Still others passed their knowledge on, building schools and monasteries around them.
P	To create an adept, start with the stats above. Pick or roll for an instinct and 1-4 moves to represent their capabilities.
PAGE	329
P	1d12 instinct
HR
P	1-2 To atone
P	3-4 To avoid disruption or distraction
P	5-6 To drive their students towards perfection
P	7-8 To prove their superiority
P	9-10 To tame chaos
P	11-12 To test themselves or their students
P	<b>1d12</b> move

ICON	icons/undead.svg
H3	False adept
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks organs)
P	<b>Damage</b> life-draining touch d8 (<i>hand</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to some object; telepathic; powerful will <b>Instinct</b> to amass more followers, more power
P	• Attract followers with promises of greatness, easily achieved
P	• Eat away at someone's emotions/ memories/will
P	• Possess a follower (or one's corpse)
P	• Siphon a follower's lifeforce to mimic some art of the Rime Lords
P	Some who practice the Rime Lord's teachings push themselves beyond their limits.
P	Their bodies fail but they become ragefilled <b>specters</b> (page 79) or ever-hungry <b>wraiths</b> (page 79). The Rime Lords had many techniques for dealing with such abominations.
P	Imagine, though, an adept who saw their body and their life as a resource to expend rather than a liability to overcome. One who burned health and vitality to empower their practice. One who saw vast, unused potential in those around them. Such an adept might deliberately sever their mind and spirit from their body and gather a herd of followers (victims) around them, to serve as fuel for their mighty arts.

H3	Rime Lord
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>magical</i> <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 26; <b>Armor</b> 5 (potent wards, skill)
P	<b>Damage</b> conjured ice d12+3 (any range, <i>area</i> <i>forceful</i>) or heat-drain d12+1 (<i>reach</i> <b>Special Qualities</b> spirit sight; telepathic; cold-proof; ageless; no need to eat/drink/sleep/breathe; aura of bitter cold <b>Instinct</b> to seek perfection (in themselves, in their surroundings, in others)
P	• Overawe those in its presence
P	• Act simultaneously in both the physical and spirit worlds
P	• Impose its mighty will on the world: stilling emotions, freezing time, dismissing magic, reshaping reality, etc.
P	• Create a tulpa or thoughtform
P	Only thirteen Rime Lords survive; each remains in stasis in some key place of power. Their spirits are merged in an eternal dance and song, continuously weaving the dark ice glacier that keeps the voice of Y'aaw'kara bound and prevents madness from spreading unchecked across the world.
P	Pray, o mortal. Pray that they continue their vigil. Pray that their wills do not falter. Pray that no interloper is so foolish as to disturb them. Pray for your family, your friends, and all that you know.
P	Pray that they do not wake.
